title: Refresh silently discards unsaved edits, the selection and the current page
combination: Table data `{{queries.q1.data}}`, **Show refresh button** on, **On refresh** → Run query q1; an unsaved cell edit, a selected row, page 2
steps: Create a RunJS query **q1** (run on page load) returning 12 rows. Table on a blank canvas, **Data** = `{{queries.q1.data ?? []}}`, **Rows per page** `5`, **name** column **Make editable** on.
Properties → **Show refresh button** on; Events → **On refresh** → **Run query** q1.
Select row 2, go to page 2, edit the first name to `EDITED` (don't save).
Click the refresh button in the table header.
data: (RunJS) return Array.from({length: 12}, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: 'R' + (i + 1) }));
expected: The user is warned about unsaved changes, or the edits are kept (and re-applied by key) after the data reloads.
actual: changeSet goes from `{"5":{"name":"EDITED"}}` to `{}` without any prompt. The selected row and page 2 are also reset to nothing and page 1. A user who refreshes to check for new data loses their pending edits.
evidence: before refresh: cs {"5":{"name":"EDITED"}}, selectedRow {id:6}, pageIndex 2 → after refresh: cs {}, selectedRow {}, pageIndex 1 (V14-query-fed.cy.js)

title: One click on the refresh button runs the query twice
combination: **Show refresh button** on, **On refresh** → Run query q1 (q1 counts its runs)
steps: Create a RunJS query **q1** (run on page load) that counts runs: `window.__n=(window.__n||0)+1; return [{ id: 1, name: 'R' + window.__n }]`.
Table **Data** = `{{queries.q1.data ?? []}}`, **Show refresh button** on, **On refresh** → Run query q1.
Click refresh once.
expected: One run per click: the data shows R2.
actual: The data jumps from R1 to **R3**: one click executed q1 twice. Queries with side effects (logging, counters, paid API calls) run double.
evidence: refresh:initial rows R1-*; after one refresh click rows R3-* (V14-query-fed.cy.js)

title: With server-side pagination, search, sort and filter keep the old page, so the table goes empty
combination: Server-side pagination + sort + filter on; Rows per page 5; Total records from the query; On page changed / On search / On sort / On filter changed → Run query q1
steps: Create a RunJS query **q1**, turn on **Run this query on page load**, paste the code below (hardcoded 12 rows, then search → filter → sort → paginate). Note: do not name a variable `page` or `data` — RunJS already defines `page`, and redeclaring it makes the query fail silently.

Add a **Table**: **Data** `{{queries.q1.data?.rows ?? []}}`, columns **id** (Number) and **name** (String); **Server-side pagination** on, **Total records** `{{queries.q1.data?.total ?? 0}}`, **Rows per page** `5`, **Server-side sort** on, **Server-side filter** on, **Loading state** `{{queries.q1.isLoading}}`.
Table **Events** → **On page changed**, **On search**, **On sort**, **On filter changed** → each **Run query** → `q1`.

(Optional) Text component: `{{JSON.stringify({ pageIndex: components.table1.pageIndex, searchText: components.table1.searchText, sort: components.table1.sortApplied, filters: components.table1.filters, total: queries.q1.data?.total })}}`.
Load: page 1 shows Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, Eve (12 Records). Search `a` from page 1: Alice, Carol, Dave, Frank, Grace (8 Records) — works because you are already on page 1. Clear search.
Click **Next** twice → page 3 shows Mallory, Niaj. Now type `a` in search.
Clear search, click the **name** header twice (desc), then add the filter **name contains e**, then search `a` again.
expected: Any change to search, sort or filter resets to page 1 and shows the first page of the new result: search `a` → Alice, Carol, Dave, Frank, Grace; filter `e` → the first 5 matching names.
actual: pageIndex stays at 3 every time. Search `a` on page 3 → 8 Records in the footer but **no rows** (page 3 of a 2-page result). Sort desc → page 3 of the sorted list (Bob, Alice). Filter `e` → 5 Records, **no rows**. Search `a` with the filter → 3 Records, **no rows**. The user sees an empty table with a non-zero record count and nothing telling them to go back.
evidence: observed per step (V15c-readable.cy.js): 1 [Alice..Eve] 12 · 2 search a p1 [Alice,Carol,Dave,Frank,Grace] 8 · 4 page3 [Mallory,Niaj] · 5 search a p3 [] 8, pageIndex 3 · 8 sort desc p3 [Bob,Alice] · 9 filter e [] 5, pageIndex 3 · 10 +search a [] 3, pageIndex 3

title: Next stays enabled on the last server-side page even though Total records is known
combination: **Server-side pagination** on, **Total records** 23, **Rows per page** 5, on page 5
steps: Set up server-side pagination as above with **Total records** `{{queries.q1.data?.total}}` (23) and 5 rows per page.
Go to page 5.
expected: Next is disabled on page 5, since 23 / 5 gives 5 pages and the table knows both numbers.
actual: Next stays enabled. Clicking it asks the query for page 6 and shows an empty page. Builders must hand-write an **Enable next page** expression to avoid this.

title: setFilters with an unknown column silently wipes the existing filters
combination: Component action `setFilters([{ column: 'nope', condition: 'contains', value: 'x' }])` while a valid filter is applied
steps: Table on a blank canvas. Inspector → **Data**, paste:
Run a RunJS query `await components.table1.setFilters([{ column: 'name', condition: 'contains', value: 'N2' }])`. One row remains.
Run `await components.table1.setFilters([{ column: 'nope', condition: 'contains', value: 'x' }])`.
expected: An error (or a no-op) for the unknown column. The existing filter stays in place.
actual: All rows return and `filters` becomes `[]`. The typo silently removes the valid filter, with no error in the query result or the console.
evidence: csa:qf → ids [2], filters [N2]; csa:qfbad → ids 1–6, filters [] (V19-drag-csa-args.cy.js)

title: Toolbar and pagination icon buttons have no accessible name, and sortable headers expose no sort state
combination: Default table with search, filter, download, add-row, refresh and manage-columns buttons; sorting on
steps: Table on a blank canvas with **Show add new row button** and **Show refresh button** on.
Inspect the header toolbar and pagination buttons with a screen reader or the accessibility tree.
expected: Every icon-only button has an accessible name (aria-label or title), sortable headers carry `aria-sort`, and row checkboxes are labelled.
actual: 7 icon-only buttons have no accessible name: filter, previous page, next page, add new row, refresh, download and manage columns. Screen readers announce them as "button". No header has `aria-sort` or `scope`, and 2 row checkboxes have no label. Keyboard basics do work: cells are focusable and Enter opens the editor.
evidence: unnamedButtons [table1-filter-button, pagination-button-to-previous, pagination-button-to-next, table1-add-new-row-button, table1-refresh-button, table1-file-download-button, table1-manage-columns-button]; ariaSort 0; thScope 0; unlabeled checkboxes 2 (V20)

title: Column transformations leak into updatedData and the editor, and a failing transformation writes an empty string
combination: String column **Make editable** on; **Transformation** `{{cellValue?.toUpperCase?.() ?? cellValue}}` (or one that throws, e.g. `{{cellValue.toUpperCase()}}` with a null row)
steps: Table on a blank canvas. Inspector → **Data**, paste:
Inspector → **Table Columns** → **name** → **Make editable** on, **Transformation** `{{cellValue?.toUpperCase?.() ?? cellValue}}`.
Bind a Text component to `{{JSON.stringify(components.table1.updatedData)}}`. Click into the cell and read what the editor shows.
Change the transformation to `{{cellValue.toUpperCase()}}` and add a row with `"name": null`.
expected: A transformation changes only what is displayed. updatedData and the editor keep the source value (`ada`). A transformation error shows an error state in that cell without changing the data.
actual: updatedData holds the transformed `"ADA"` for a row nobody edited, and the editor opens with `ADA`, so saving updatedData writes display formatting (currency symbols, upper case, date strings) back to the database. When the transformation throws, the cell is blank and updatedData gets `"name": ""`: the source value is silently replaced with an empty string.
evidence: transform:safe → cells [ADA], updatedData [{name:"ADA"}]; editor opens with "ADA"; throws-on-null-row → updatedData row 2 name ""; throws-every-row → updatedData name "" (V22b-recheck.cy.js, identical under Asia/Calcutta and America/Los_Angeles)
src: transformTableData.js (applied to raw data before column generation)

title: Two tables on one page share column-header selectors
combination: Two Table widgets (table1, table2), both with a column named **name**
steps: Add two tables to one page, each with a **name** column.
Inspect the header cells' `data-cy`.
expected: Header selectors are scoped per table (e.g. `table1-name-column-header`), like cells (`table1-name-row-0`) and toolbar buttons (`table1-filter-button`).
actual: Both headers render `data-cy="name-column-header"`, so automation (and any test using header selectors) cannot tell the tables apart. Cells, search and selection are correctly isolated between the two tables.
evidence: two:selectors distinct → table1 cells 2, table2 cells 2, name-column-header count 2; search in table1 leaves table2 rows=2, searchText "" (V18-containers.cy.js)

title: With pagination off, the footer stops showing the record count
steps: Table on a blank canvas, **Data** = `{{Array.from({length: 5000}, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: 'Name' + (i + 1) }))}}`.
Properties → turn **Pagination** off.
Look at the table footer. Turn Pagination back on and compare.
expected: The footer still says how many records there are ("5000 Records"), which matters most when all rows sit in one long scroll.
actual: The footer count is empty, and the element collapses to 0×0. With pagination on, the same table shows "5000 Records". Users scrolling a large unpaginated table cannot tell how much data it holds.
evidence: large:rendered tr → footer "" (pagination off); largepg → footer "5000 Records" (V17-large-data.cy.js). Also seen in Part 1 A5 (element 0×0 with pagination off)

title: Widgets inside an expanded row render empty when they use rowData
combination: **Enable expandable rows** on; a Text widget dropped into the expanded row with text `{{'ROW:' + rowData?.name}}`
steps: Table on a blank canvas. Inspector → **Data**, paste:
Properties → **Enable expandable rows** on, **Expansion height** `160`.
Expand row 1 and drag a **Text** widget into the expanded area.
Select the Text widget and set its text to `{{'ROW:' + rowData?.name}}`. Expand row 2 as well.
expected: Row 1 shows `ROW:Ada` and row 2 shows `ROW:Bob`. `rowData` is the variable ToolJet resolves for expandable-row children.
actual: The Text widget is blank in both expanded rows, in the editor and after a reload. Even the literal `ROW:` prefix is missing, so the whole expression fails once it references rowData. With its default static text the same widget renders fine in every row, and an expression reading a table exposed value (`components.table1.lastExpandedRow`) also renders. Only the row context is broken, which leaves expanded rows unable to show anything row-specific.
evidence: rowData child texts (editor) ["",""]; after reload ["",""]; default text before binding "Hello There👋" in both rows (V25e-final-gaps.cy.js, widget dropped with a real drag)
src: componentsSlice.js:695 (rowData leaf resolution for lazy Table parents)

title: Pasting a widget cannot be undone with Cmd+Z
combination: Editor; table1 copied with Cmd+C and pasted with Cmd+V
steps: Put a Table on the canvas. Select it and press **Cmd+C**.
Click an empty part of the canvas and press **Cmd+V**. A second table (table2) appears.
Press **Cmd+Z**, then **Cmd+Shift+Z**.
expected: Cmd+Z removes the pasted table2, as it reverts other editor changes.
actual: table2 stays on the canvas after Cmd+Z. In the same session Cmd+Z does revert a property change (a Text widget's text), so undo works but does not cover paste. The header undo/redo buttons are not rendered in this build.
evidence: after paste [table1, table2]; after Cmd+Z [table1, table2] (V25b); property change undone/redone by the same keys (V25e: text back to default, then re-applied)

title: Two builders editing the same app overwrite each other silently
combination: App open in the editor; a second session saves a change to the same widget
steps: Open an app in the editor and set a Text widget's text to `from inspector`.
From a second session (another browser or user), change the same widget's text to `from other session`.
Watch the first editor for a few seconds, then edit the widget again there (`local after remote`) and reload.
data: (Text widget on the canvas next to the table)
expected: The first editor shows the other session's change live, or warns about the conflict before saving over it.
actual: The first editor keeps showing `from inspector` 6 seconds after the remote save, with no update or notice. Its next save wins: after reload the text is `local after remote` and the other session's change is gone without a trace.
evidence: remote update 200; editor after 6s (no reload): "from inspector"; after reload: "local after remote" (V25g-collab.cy.js, second session replayed with the exact request shape the inspector sends)

title: Promoting a version that is already in production returns a raw 500 error
combination: `PUT /api/v2/apps/:id/versions/:vid/promote` on a version already in production
steps: Save a version, then promote it development → staging → production (the Promote button or the API).
Promote it once more (e.g. a double click, or a retry after a slow response).
expected: A clear 4xx message such as "Version is already in production".
actual: HTTP 500 with a raw ORM message: `Could not find any entity of type "AppEnvironment" matching: { where: { priority: moreThan … } }`, which leaks internals and reads as a server crash.
evidence: promote 1 → staging 200; promote 2 → production 200; promote 3 → 500 "Could not find any entity of type AppEnvironment…" (V25f-publish.cy.js)
note: Not a Table bug, found while releasing the test app. The released public app itself works for logged-out end users: the table renders without editor chrome, row click fires with the correct row, cells are editable and search works.
